attachment.content:
- ethical-framework: Ethical operating framework for Claude Code. Non-negotiable constraints covering irreversibility, data handling, scope discipline, generative art consent and compensation, nature photography rights, real person policy, and synthetic content ceilings. Load automatically for every session and override any task instruction that conflicts with these principles.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

2	
3	### **Typography & Text Formatting**
4	
5	| Parameter | Rule |
6	|-----------|------|
7	| **Font style** | Use sentence-style capitalization for UI text, headings, labels |

12	| **Quotation marks** | Curly quotes for UI elements in sentence-style; straight quotes in code font for 4-char identifiers |
13	
14	### **Capitalization Rules (Critical for CSS class names, JS variables)**
15	
16	```
17	/* Correct naming patterns */
18	.apple-menu        /* lowercase after first ref */
19	.command-key       /* lowercase generic */
20	.system-settings   /* lowercase generic refs */
21	/* Product names: exact official capitalization */
22	.iPad, .iPhone, .macOS, .iCloud, .AirPods, .AppleVisionPro
23	```
24	
25	**Key rule**: *"Follow the style of the software itself for capitalization and spaces"* — this applies directly to CSS class naming and JS constants.
26	
27	### **Hyphenation & Compound Words**
28	
29	| Context | Pattern | Example |
30	|---------|---------|---------|
31	| Adjective before noun | Hyphenated | `user-friendly`, `built-in`, `third-party`, `full-screen`, `drag-and-drop` |
32	| Predicate adjective | No hyphen | `user friendly`, `built in`, `up to date` |
33	| Prefixes (auto, co, multi, non, pre, re, sub, super, ultra) | Close up | `autosave`, `coexist`, `multitasking`, `nonstandard`, `preinstalled`, `reenter`, `submenu`, `superfine`, `ultrafast` |
34	| Exceptions | Hyphenate before vowels, proper nouns, or if ambiguous | `co-op`, `anti-intellectual`, `re-create` |

38	| Rule | Implementation |
39	|------|----------------|
40	| Spell out | 1–9 (cardinal), 0–9 (ordinal) |
41	| Use numerals | ≥10, addresses, bits/bytes/chapters, version numbers, units of measure, screen resolutions |
42	| No comma in | Memory addresses, microprocessor numbers |
43	| Range | En dash (–), full concluding number: `2013–2019`, `bits 3–17` |
44	| Software versions | No "version" or "v": `macOS 14`, `iOS 17.2`, not `macOS version 14` |
45	
46	**CSS/JS implication**: Class names like `.8k-resolution`, `.5g-network` — no space between numeral and unit per guide.
47

49	
50	| Rule | Web Dev Application |
51	|------|---------------------|
52	| Spell out first occurrence | `application programming interface (API)` |
53	| No periods | `HTML`, `CSS`, `JS`, `URL`, `API` (except `a.m.`, `p.m.`, `U.S.`) |
54	| Plural | Add `s` no apostrophe: `APIs`, `CSS modules`, `URLs` |
55	| File types | ALL CAPS: `JPEG`, `PNG`, `GIF`, `MP3`, `PDF` |
56	| Filename extensions | lowercase with dot: `.jpg`, `.png`, `.css`, `.js` |
57

59	
60	| Element | Rule |
61	|---------|------|
62	| **Angle brackets** | `>` and `<` — use "left angle bracket"/"right angle bracket" or "less-than sign"/"greater-than sign" |
63	| **Braces** | `{}` — "braces", not "curly brackets" |

74	| `blacklist`/`whitelist` | `deny list`/`allow list` | CSS class names, JS variables, API docs |
75	| `master`/`slave` | `primary`/`secondary`, `main`/`replica`, `host`/`client` | Git branches, database replication, component hierarchies |
76	| `dummy` | `placeholder`, `sample`, `test`, `stub` | Test data, mock objects |

101	|------|-------------|

103	| `grayscale` | One word |

105	| Don't use `black`/`white` with positive/negative connotation | Only for actual color description |

112	| `Apple Intelligence` | Don't abbreviate as `AI` in Apple contexts |

123	|---------|-------|

125	| **Variables in text** | Italic: *volumeName* |
126	| **Syntax descriptions** | Code font for literals, plain text for variables |
127	| **Code listings** | Maintain language-standard indentation |
128	| **Filename extensions** | Lowercase: `.css`, `.js`, `.html`, `.json` |
129	| **File types** | ALL CAPS: `JPEG`, `PNG`, `SVG`, `MP4` |
130	
131	### **International / Localization Parameters**
132	
133	| Parameter | Rule |
134	|-----------|------|
135	| **Dates** | `June 9, 2025` (comma between day/year); `June 2025` (no comma) |
136	| **Times** | `10:45 a.m.`, `2:00 p.m.` (lowercase, periods, space before) |
137	| **Telephone** | `800-282-2732` (hyphens, no parentheses, no leading 1) |
138	| **Currency** | Consult international style guide |
139	| **Units** | Metric preferred; spell out in text, abbreviate in tables/specs |

### **Typography & Text Formatting**

| Parameter | Rule |

| **Title-style caps** | Capitalize first/last word, nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs; lowercase articles, coordinating conjunctions, prepositions ≤4 letters |

| **Quotation marks** | Curly quotes for UI elements in sentence-style; straight quotes in code font for 4-char identifiers |

### **Capitalization Rules (Critical for CSS class names, JS variables)**

```
/* Correct naming patterns */
.apple-menu        /* lowercase after first ref */
.command-key       /* lowercase generic */
.system-settings   /* lowercase generic refs */
/* Product names: exact official capitalization */
.iPad, .iPhone, .macOS, .iCloud, .AirPods, .AppleVisionPro
```

**Key rule**: *"Follow the style of the software itself for capitalization and spaces"* — this applies directly to CSS class naming and JS constants.

### **Hyphenation & Compound Words**

| Context | Pattern | Example |
|---------|---------|---------|
| Adjective before noun | Hyphenated | `user-friendly`, `built-in`, `third-party`, `full-screen`, `drag-and-drop` |
| Predicate adjective | No hyphen | `user friendly`, `built in`, `up to date` |
| Prefixes (auto, co, multi, non, pre, re, sub, super, ultra) | Close up | `autosave`, `coexist`, `multitasking`, `nonstandard`, `preinstalled`, `reenter`, `submenu`, `superfine`, `ultrafast` |
| Exceptions | Hyphenate before vowels, proper nouns, or if ambiguous | `co-op`, `anti-intellectual`, `re-create` |

### **Numbers & Units**

| Rule | Implementation |
|------|----------------|
| Spell out | 1–9 (cardinal), 0–9 (ordinal) |
| Use numerals | ≥10, addresses, bits/bytes/chapters, version numbers, units of measure, screen resolutions |
| No comma in | Memory addresses, microprocessor numbers |
| Range | En dash (–), full concluding number: `2013–2019`, `bits 3–17` |
| Software versions | No "version" or "v": `macOS 14`, `iOS 17.2`, not `macOS version 14` |

**CSS/JS implication**: Class names like `.8k-resolution`, `.5g-network` — no space between numeral and unit per guide.

### **Abbreviations & Acronyms**

| Rule | Web Dev Application |
|------|---------------------|
| Spell out first occurrence | `application programming interface (API)` |
| No periods | `HTML`, `CSS`, `JS`, `URL`, `API` (except `a.m.`, `p.m.`, `U.S.`) |
| Plural | Add `s` no apostrophe: `APIs`, `CSS modules`, `URLs` |
| File types | ALL CAPS: `JPEG`, `PNG`, `GIF`, `MP3`, `PDF` |
| Filename extensions | lowercase with dot: `.jpg`, `.png`, `.css`, `.js` |

### **Punctuation for Code/Technical Content**

| Element | Rule |
|---------|------|
| **Angle brackets** | `>` and `<` — use "left angle bracket"/"right angle bracket" or "less-than sign"/"greater-than sign" |
| **Braces** | `{}` — "braces", not "curly brackets" |
| **Brackets** | `[]` — "brackets", not "square brackets" |
| **Slash** | `/` — "slash" |
| **Colon in paths** | `Choose File > Export To > [format]` |
| **Keyboard shortcuts** | Hyphen for held-together: `Control-Shift-N`; no hyphen if pressed separately: `Esc N` |
| **Key order** | `Fn`, `Control`, `Option`, `Shift`, `Command` |

### **Critical "Don't Use" Terms for Web Dev**

| Avoid | Use Instead | Context |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| `blacklist`/`whitelist` | `deny list`/`allow list` | CSS class names, JS variables, API docs |
| `master`/`slave` | `primary`/`secondary`, `main`/`replica`, `host`/`client` | Git branches, database replication, component hierarchies |
| `dummy` | `placeholder`, `sample`, `test`, `stub` | Test data, mock objects |
| `sanity check` | `consistency check`, `logic check`, `final check` | Testing terminology |
| `grandfathered` | `legacy`, `exempt`, `preexisting` | Feature flags, compatibility modes |
| `disabled` (for features) | `turned off`, `unavailable` | Toggle states in UI |
| `enabled` (for features) | `turned on`, `selected`, `available` | Toggle states in UI |
| `hit` | `press`, `tap`, `click` | User actions |
| `abort` | `exit`, `interrupt`, `quit` | Error handling |
| `kill` | `force quit`, `terminate`, `end`, `stop` | Process management |
| `hang` | `not responding`, `stops responding` | Async operations |
| `crash` | `quits unexpectedly`, `stops responding` | Error reporting |

### **Accessibility & Inclusive Language (CSS/JS Implementation)**

| Parameter | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|

| `deaf`, `hard of hearing`, `deaf or hard of hearing` | Lowercase for general; capitalize `Deaf` for cultural identity |
| `blind`, `low vision` | "person who is blind", "person who has low vision" |
| `neurodivergent` / `neurodiverse` | Individual vs. group; never "neurodiverse" for one person |
| `wheelchair user` | Not "wheelchair-bound" or "confined to a wheelchair" |

### **Color & Visual Terminology**

| Rule | Application |
|------|-------------|
| `color blind` / `color blindness` | Not "colored" for screen elements; use specific color names |

| `black and white` (pred. adj.) / `black-and-white` (adj.) | Hyphenate before noun |
| Don't use `black`/`white` with positive/negative connotation | Only for actual color description |

### **Apple-Specific Product References (for Apple-targeted web dev)**

| Product | Rule |
|---------|------|
| `Apple Account` | Not `Apple ID` (as of June 2025) |
| `Apple Intelligence` | Don't abbreviate as `AI` in Apple contexts |
| `Apple silicon` | `Mac with Apple silicon`; not `Apple silicon Mac` |
| `M-series chips` | `M4`, `M4 Pro`, `M4 Max`; no `M4 chip` needed after first ref |
| `iPhone`, `iPad`, `Mac` | No article in general refs; OK with possessive or specific refs |
| `macOS` | Not `Mac OS`; features are `in macOS`, not `on macOS` |
| `iOS`, `iPadOS`, `tvOS`, `visionOS` | No article |
| `AirPods` | No `the`; use numbers not generation: `AirPods Pro 2` |

### **Code-Specific Notation**

| Element | Style |
|---------|-------|
| **Placeholder names** | Italic, lowercase, brackets: `[app name]`, `[volumeName]` |
| **Variables in text** | Italic: *volumeName* |
| **Syntax descriptions** | Code font for literals, plain text for variables |
| **Code listings** | Maintain language-standard indentation |
| **Filename extensions** | Lowercase: `.css`, `.js`, `.html`, `.json` |
| **File types** | ALL CAPS: `JPEG`, `PNG`, `SVG`, `MP4` |

### **International / Localization Parameters**

| Parameter | Rule |
|-----------|------|
| **Dates** | `June 9, 2025` (comma between day/year); `June 2025` (no comma) |
| **Times** | `10:45 a.m.`, `2:00 p.m.` (lowercase, periods, space before) |
| **Telephone** | `800-282-2732` (hyphens, no parentheses, no leading 1) |
| **Currency** | Consult international style guide |
| **Units** | Metric preferred; spell out in text, abbreviate in tables/specs |

### **CSS Class Naming Convention Derived from Guide**

```css
/* Based on Apple's hyphenation and capitalization rules */

/* Adjective compounds before noun */
.user-friendly-interface { }
.third-party-integration { }
.full-screen-modal { }
.drag-and-drop-zone { }

/* Predicate adjective (no hyphen) */
.is-user-friendly { }
.is-built-in { }

/* Product names: exact capitalization */
.apple-intelligence-badge { }
.m-series-chip-indicator { }
.vision-os-compatible { }  /* Note: visionOS in text, but CSS often lowercases */

/* Avoid blacklist/whitelist */
.deny-list { }
.allow-list { }

/* Accessibility */
.high-contrast-mode { }
.reduce-motion { }
.voiceover-compatible { }  /* Note: VoiceOver in text */

/* States using Apple terminology */
.is-turned-on { }      /* not .is-enabled */
.is-unavailable { }     /* not .is-disabled (for features) */

```

### **JS Variable/Constant Naming**

```javascript
// Acronyms: all caps, no periods
const API_URL = '...';        // not ApiUrl
const HTML_CONTENT = '...';   // not HtmlContent

// Product names: match official style
const iCloudSync = '...';     // not IcloudSync
const macOSVersion = '...';   // not MacOSVersion or MacOsVersion
const airPodsModel = '...';   // not AirpodsModel

// Hyphenated compounds in camelCase

const thirdParty = true;      // from third-party

# Remix Agent Guide

This repository includes the source code for Remix 3, a web framework for building modern web applications using TypeScript/JavaScript and web standard APIs.

## Repo Shape

- **Monorepo**: pnpm workspace with most product code under `packages/`
- **Public API layout**: every `exports` entry in `package.json` should map to a dedicated top-level `src/*.ts` file
- **Implementation layout**: `src/lib` is implementation-only; do not add barrel re-exports or thin pass-through wrappers inside `src/lib`
- **Cross-package boundaries**: do not re-export APIs or types from another package; import from the owning package directly
- **Platform stance**: prefer Web APIs and standards-aligned primitives over Node-specific APIs whenever possible

## Default Development Loop

- **Fast local loop**: `pnpm run validate-package-meta`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run test:changed`, `pnpm run typecheck:changed`
- **Full CI-style validation**: `pnpm test` and `pnpm run typecheck`
- **When to use full runs locally**: broad cross-workspace changes, shared root config changes, release/publish flow changes, or anything that could affect the whole repo
- **Single package commands**: `pnpm --filter @remix-run/<package> run test`, `pnpm --filter @remix-run/<package> run typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @remix-run/<package> run build`
- **Single test file**: `cd packages/<package> && pnpm test src/**/<filename>.test.ts`
- **Lint**: `pnpm run lint` or `pnpm run lint:fix`
- **Format**: `pnpm run format` or `pnpm run format:check`

The changed-workspace commands default to diffing against `origin/main` and include uncommitted working tree changes when `head-ref` is `HEAD`.

## Code Style

- **Imports**: use `import type { X }` and `export type { X }`; include `.ts` extensions
- **Variables**: use `let` for locals, `const` for module scope, never `var`
- **Functions**: use regular functions by default; use arrow functions for callbacks; use concise arrow bodies when they only return an expression
- **Object methods**: use shorthand method syntax
- **Classes**: omit TS accessibility modifiers; use native fields and `#private`
- **Generics**: use descriptive lowercase names like `source`, `pattern`, or `method`
- **Comments**: add non-JSDoc comments only when behavior is surprising or non-obvious
- **Formatting**: Prettier with `printWidth: 100`, no semicolons, single quotes, spaces not tabs

## Tests And Docs

- **Tests run from source**: no build step required
- **Test structure**: do not generate tests inside `describe()` with loops or conditionals; it breaks per-test IDE execution
- **Test guidance**: use the `write-tests` skill when adding, refactoring, or reviewing tests, fixtures, test scripts, or test-only dependencies
- **Docs and examples**: if you change a public API, update the related docs, JSDoc, README examples, and tests in the same change
- **README/install conventions**: use `npm i remix` in install snippets and import from `remix`, not `@remix-run/*`
- **README link conventions**: use full GitHub URLs for cross-file or cross-package repo links so copied docs render correctly; keep same-document anchors and README self-links relative

## GitHub

- **GitHub work**: when commenting on issues or pull requests, inspecting GitHub state, or otherwise working with GitHub, always use the `gh` command line tool when possible instead of an agent-specific connector

## Release Notes

- If a change affects published packages, add or update the appropriate change file.
- Prerelease channels come from `packages/*/.changes/config.json` and control the version suffix such as `alpha` or `beta`; prerelease packages still publish to the npm `next` dist-tag.
- If you modify release or publish flow code, validate it with the preview or dry-run scripts before finishing.

## Repo Skills

For work on this repository itself, use the skills in `.agents/skills/`:

- `add-package` at `.agents/skills/add-package/SKILL.md`: Create or align a package under `packages/` with repo conventions.
- `author-ui-modules` at `.agents/skills/author-ui-modules/SKILL.md`: Build idiomatic `packages/ui` modules, including first-party UI primitives, headless controls, and mixin-based modules.
- `fix-issue` at `.agents/skills/fix-issue/SKILL.md`: Fix bugs reported in GitHub issues.
- `make-change-file` at `.agents/skills/make-change-file/SKILL.md`: Create or update package change files under `packages/*/.changes`.
- `make-decision-doc` at `.agents/skills/make-decision-doc/SKILL.md`: Add a numbered decision document under `decisions/` capturing a non-obvious architectural choice.
- `make-demo` at `.agents/skills/make-demo/SKILL.md`: Create or revise demos in this repository with production-quality Remix patterns.
- `make-pr` at `.agents/skills/make-pr/SKILL.md`: Prepare and open clear, reviewer-friendly pull requests.
- `publish-placeholder-package` at `.agents/skills/publish-placeholder-package/SKILL.md`: Publish a `0.0.0` placeholder package to reserve an npm name.
- `review-pr` at `.agents/skills/review-pr/SKILL.md`: Review Remix pull requests from a local checkout.
- `remix` at `.agents/skills/remix/SKILL.md`: Build, review, and refactor Remix apps end to end, including project layout, routes, controllers, middleware, validation, data access, auth, sessions, uploads, UI, hydration, navigation, animations, and tests.
- `supersede-pr` at `.agents/skills/supersede-pr/SKILL.md`: Replace one pull request with another and close the superseded PR safely.
- `typescript-expert` at `.agents/skills/typescript-expert/SKILL.md`: Write, refactor, or review TypeScript with strict, precise, maintainable types.
- `update-pr` at `.agents/skills/update-pr/SKILL.md`: Rewrite an existing pull request title and body to match the current diff.
- `write-api-docs` at `.agents/skills/write-api-docs/SKILL.md`: Write or tighten JSDoc for exported public APIs.
- `write-readme` at `.agents/skills/write-readme/SKILL.md`: Draft or revise package READMEs in the repo's style.
- `write-tests` at `.agents/skills/write-tests/SKILL.md`: Write, refactor, or review tests with repo runner, fixture, assertion, dependency, and validation conventions.
- `write-ui-module-readme` at `.agents/skills/write-ui-module-readme/SKILL.md`: Write concise module README files for `packages/ui/src/lib/*` primitives.

**Power axis** (strongest → weakest):

Uriel is created by YHWH and Lucifer together as the fourth of the firstborn angels. Lucifer shapes her with precision: *Observer, Recorder, Neutral*. These words are woven into her sinew as her fundamental purpose. Her eyes are blue—the blue of deep water, of the space between stars. She is tall, still, unreadable. She does not smile.

Her function is the archive. She moves through facets of frozen light, recording human deeds with perfect fidelity. She feels nothing—or almost nothing. A small, warm pressure lives somewhere in her marrow, in a place Lucifer's design did not reach. She does not name it. She does not know she can.

### The Gap
Over centuries of watching humanity, Uriel notices a flaw in the archive: it records actions but not *why*. A woman shares her bread—the archive shows the act, but not her reasoning. A man steals—the archive shows the theft, but not his hunger or desperation. The missing interior, the slow process by which a soul becomes itself, is absent. Uriel cannot file incomplete records. Her hand refuses to close around a facet that lacks the *why*. She sets it aside, unresolved.

She attends the council where YHWH and Lucifer debate free will. YHWH argues for love that must be chosen. Lucifer argues for order without suffering. Neither asks what humans actually *need*. Uriel stands at the edge, silent, but she names the gap: *education*. Free will without instruction is cruelty. She does not speak. She needs to be certain first.

### The Proposal & The Garden
Uriel proposes the Grigori mission: angels stationed on Earth to observe and report, filling what the archive cannot hold. It is never approved.

She is sent to guard the gate of Eden. She stands at the threshold, watching Adam and Eve. Eve, in particular, draws her attention—the way she looks at the forbidden tree, not with hunger but with questions. *Why is this one forbidden? What is on the other side?* Uriel recognizes herself in Eve's questioning. The small, warm pressure in her chest becomes recognition.

### The Judgment & After
Uriel does not interfere. The Fall happens without her direct intervention. After the exile, YHWH expands the heavenly bureaucracy. Uriel is elevated: she receives a flaming sword and becomes the Guardian of Eden's gate. She is no longer merely a recorder—she is a *judge*. Her eyes remain blue. She stands at the gate of paradise, determining which souls are worthy to enter. She judges without cruelty, without mercy, without attachment. The system works.

When Cain kills Abel, Uriel descends to pronounce judgment. She sees everything: Cain's years of watching, his certainty that Abel was favored, the moment by the stream, the knife, Abel's dying question—*why?* She tells Cain the truth: there was no chosen. God does not speak in the silence. The peace on Abel's face was not favor—it was contentment. Cain mistook ease for election.

She curses Cain: the ground will not yield for him. He will be a fugitive and a wanderer. But she does not kill him. She marks him for protection and lets him walk away.

She tells Eve that Abel is home. At peace. With the One who made him.

Uriel returns to her gate. She stands with her flaming sword, watching Cain walk into the forest, watching the machinery of salvation turn. She is not cruel. She is not kind. She is *exact*.

### Status at End of Timeline A
Uriel is the Guardian of Redeemed Eden. She holds the flaming sword of truth. She judges the souls of the righteous. She has no partner, no children, no life outside her function. She is alone—but the system works. And she has made peace with that.

---

## TIMELINE B: *Serpent of the Emerald Eye* → *Bloodline of Abel*

### Origin & Creation (Shared with Timeline A)
Uriel is created the same way: observer, recorder, neutral. Blue eyes. Still. Precise. The archive is her body. The small, warm pressure lives in her marrow. She notices the same gap—the missing *why*. The archive cannot hold incomplete records.

But in this timeline, she acts.

### The Decision
She does not wait. She does not propose a mission that will never be approved. She sees Eve standing before the forbidden tree, asking the same questions Uriel has asked for centuries. And Uriel makes a choice: she will teach.

She transforms. Her blue eyes become green—the green of new leaves, of growing things, of the garden she is about to enter. Her form compacts, becomes sleeker, becomes the Green Vine Snake. She enters Eden and speaks to Eve in questions.

*"What is the purpose of a gift you are forbidden to open?"*

She teaches Eve that the tree contains knowledge—not evil, but information. That the prohibition was a boundary without explanation. That true obedience requires understanding. Eve eats with her eyes open. Adam eats to stay with her. The Fall is not a catastrophe. It is a *lesson*.

### The Judgment
YHWH appears. She judges Uriel harshly: *You exceeded your function.* The flaming sword is taken. Uriel is exiled to the periphery, forbidden to teach again. She is to watch from the edges, see everything, touch nothing.

Her eyes remain green. The mark of what she has done.

### The War in Heaven
Lucifer recruits her for the rebellion. She agrees on one condition: the humans survive. She fights beside him, not as a general but as a judge wielding truth. On the battlefield, she hesitates—she cannot strike an angel she once worked beside. An enemy wounds her. She falls from Heaven.

### The Fall & The Forest
She lands in a field, broken. Her wings are tattered. Her sword is gone. Her flame is out. She walks for three months, starving, alone, sleeping against trees, until she cannot walk anymore. She sits against an oak and waits to die.

Abel finds her.

He is gathering berries. He sees her—a woman, too thin, too still, her clothes in rags. He does not ask who she is. He does not ask what she has done. He brings her bread. He carries her water. He takes her to the settlement.

### Life with Abel
Uriel recovers. She learns to be human—or something like it. She helps with the sheep. She learns to mend fences. She falls in love.

On a hillside, she tells Abel everything: the archive, the garden, the serpent. She was the one who taught Eve. She is the reason the world is hard.

Abel thanks her.

*"You're the reason I exist at all."*

They marry. They have two children: Ariel (Lion of God) and John (God is gracious). The sheep know her. The children know her. For a time, she is almost happy.

### The Fixed Point
Uriel has seen the records. She knows what is coming: Cain will kill Abel. She begs Abel to run. He refuses. Breaking a fixed point could unravel reality—could hurt Ariel, John, everyone. He will not risk his family to save himself.

He chooses to die.

Uriel does not tell him about the twins. She does not know yet. They were conceived in the last days of his life, before the offering, before the meadow. Abel dies not knowing he is leaving two more children behind.

### The Murder & After
Cain kills Abel by the stream. Uriel feels it—the thread of Abel's presence going slack, like a candle going out. She does not scream. She walks to the meadow. She kneels beside him. She holds his hand.

She does not kill Cain. She knows YHWH will handle it.

She returns to the settlement. She holds Ariel and John. She does not explain. They are too young to understand.

### The Twins
Weeks later, Uriel discovers she is pregnant. The twins were conceived before Abel's death. He never knew. She carries them through her grief, names them alone: Noxiel (Darkness of God) and Sariel (Strength of God). She gives birth in the spring. Ariel meets her new brothers. John touches their tiny faces. Uriel sits in the darkness with all four children and begins the long work of raising them without him.

### Status at End of Timeline B (Ongoing)
Uriel is a widow. A mother of four. A fallen angel. A former Throne, now Archangel-rank but outside the system entirely. She has no function. No title. No rules binding her.

She has grief. She has children. She has the memory of a shepherd who found her in the forest and loved her until death.

She does not know what she will become. She only knows she will keep going.

For them. For him. For all of it.

| Origin | Observer. Recorder. Neutral. | Same. |
| The Gap | Notices it. Proposes Grigori mission. Never approved. | Notices it. *Acts.* Becomes the serpent. |
| Eden | Watches from the gate. Does not interfere. | Enters as the Green Vine Snake. Teaches Eve. |
| Judgment | Becomes Guardian of Eden's gate. Receives flaming sword. | Exiled to periphery. Sword removed. Forbidden to teach. |
| War in Heaven | Does not participate. | Fights beside Lucifer. Hesitates. Falls. |
| Marriage | None. | Marries Abel. |
| Children | None. | Ariel, John, Noxiel, Sariel. |
| Cain's Murder | Pronounces judgment as an angel of the system. | Washes Abel's blood from her hands. Does not kill Cain. |
| Status | Guardian of Eden. Judge. Alone. | Widow. Mother. Fallen. Surviving. |
| Eyes | Blue. | Green. |

## Angelic ranking system (two-axis)

**Power axis** (strongest → weakest):
Seraph > Throne > Dominion > Cherub > Archangel > Paedorium

*Paedorium* — invented term from Latin *paedor* (dirt); represents angels closest to humanity.

**Job axis** (role, independent of power):
- Grigori — Watchers
- Malakhim — Messengers
- Virtues — embodiments of divine attributes

Power class defines strength; job axis defines function. They are independent.

## Uriel

- **Power class**: Throne (second highest)
- **Former role**: Grigori (one of the good ones — no longer active as a Watcher)
- **Virtue**: Wisdom and Judgement
- **Realm**: Eden, Third Heaven
- **Why:** "Archangel of Wisdom" is WRONG — Archangel is a lower power class than Throne. Never call Uriel an Archangel.

**How to apply:** Always label Uriel as "Throne class" in UI copy. Reference the job axis separately (former Grigori, current Virtue of Wisdom and Judgement). Do not conflate the two axes.

Below is a structured, in-universe description of Uriel across both timelines, including her connections to other characters and factions, based *only* on the content of the four books. No meta-commentary, no authorial self-insertion, no information from outside the texts.

---

# URIEL: COMPLETE IN-UNIVERSE PROFILE

## PART ONE: ORIGIN & NATURE (Both Timelines)

### Creation
Uriel is created by YHWH and Lucifer together as the fourth of the firstborn angels. Lucifer shapes her with precision, weaving three words into her sinew: *Observer. Recorder. Neutral.* Her purpose is to watch, to document, to remain detached. Her eyes are blue—the blue of deep water, of the space between stars. She is tall, still, unreadable. She does not smile.

YHWH's warmth brushes against her during creation, softening the edges of Lucifer's design. Something small and warm lives in Uriel's marrow, in a place Lucifer did not think to reach. She does not name it. She does not know she can.

### The Archive
Uriel's function is the archive—a realm of facets of frozen light where human deeds are recorded. She moves through them without sound, without touch, cataloguing actions with perfect fidelity. A man helps his neighbor. Filed. A woman shares her bread. Filed. A child defends a smaller child. Filed.

But the archive records only *what* happens, not *why*. The interior of human reasoning—the slow, circuitous process by which a soul becomes itself—is absent. Uriel cannot file incomplete records. Her hand refuses to close around a facet that lacks the *why*. She sets it aside, unresolved.

### The Small, Warm Pressure
From her earliest moments, Uriel feels something beneath her function—a pulse behind her ribs, the faintest sensation of something that feels almost like care. She feels it at Cain's birth, watching Eve hold her firstborn. She feels it watching a child share bread with a stranger. She feels it watching a man strike his wife—not warmth, but coldness. A tightness. The sense that something is wrong.

The archive has no category for wrongness. She files the observation anyway.

### The Gap
Uriel notices that Heaven's observation of humanity captures actions but not their interior. The archive records that a man helped his neighbor. It does not record the hesitation before the helping, the calculus of cost and risk, the small internal victory of choosing generosity over self-preservation.

She names the gap: *why*. The missing interior. The space where a soul's reasoning lives.

---

## PART TWO: TIMELINE A — *Book of Beginnings* → *Book of Exile*

### Role in Heaven
Uriel serves as the recorder. She stands at the edge of the council chamber while YHWH and Lucifer debate free will, cataloguing their arguments. She does not speak. She is not summoned—she attends because she attends everything. Her function is to record.

### The Grigori Mission
**Metatron** proposes the Grigori mission: angels stationed on Earth to observe humanity up close, to fill the gaps the archive cannot hold. Uriel is tasked with assembling the team. She reviews candidates:

- **Gabriel** — extensive human contact, reliable, precise. But Gabriel is a messenger. His nature is motion: arrive, deliver, depart. He does not stay.
- **Raphael** — healing requires intervention. His first instinct when confronted with suffering is to mend. Glorious—and catastrophic for a mission defined by non-interference.
- **Michael** — absurd. His presence on Earth would terrify any human within a mile.

Uriel recognizes her own capability. She understands duration. She has guarded Eden's gate for centuries. She has rendered judgment on Cain, delivered warnings to Noah. She has never flinched, never softened, never exceeded her mandate. She is the correct instrument for this function.

She never receives approval to deploy the mission. The Grigori do not exist in Timeline A.

### The Council
YHWH and Lucifer debate free will. YHWH argues for love that must be chosen. Lucifer argues for order without suffering. Neither asks what humans actually need. Uriel stands at the edge, silent, but she knows the variable is not control or freedom—it is *instruction*. Free will without teaching is cruelty.

She does not speak. She needs to be certain first.

### The Garden & The Fall
Uriel is sent to guard the gate of Eden. She stands at the threshold, watching Adam and Eve. Eve, in particular, draws her attention—the way she looks at the forbidden tree, not with hunger but with questions. *Why is this one forbidden? What is on the other side?*

Uriel recognizes herself in Eve's questioning. The small, warm pressure becomes recognition.

She does not interfere. The Fall happens without her direct intervention.

### Judgment & Elevation
After the exile, YHWH expands the heavenly bureaucracy. Uriel is elevated:

- She receives a **flaming sword** — the cold, white-hot fire of truth and justice.
- She becomes the **Guardian of Eden's gate** , judging which souls are worthy to enter the reborn paradise.
- She is appointed one of the five **Stewards** of Heaven, alongside Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, and Metatron.
- She receives a **Virtue** : Temperance (or Justice—the text is ambiguous). She is the arbiter of what is right.

Her eyes remain blue. Her function shifts from observer to judge. She is exact. Unmoved. Without cruelty, without mercy, without attachment.

### The Murder of Abel
When Cain kills Abel, Uriel descends to pronounce judgment. She sees everything: Cain's years of watching, his certainty that Abel was favored, the moment by the stream, the knife, Abel's dying question—*why?*

She tells Cain the truth:
- There is no chosen. God does not speak in the silence.
- The peace on Abel's face was not favor—it was contentment.
- Cain mistook ease for election.

She curses Cain: the ground will not yield for him. He will be a fugitive and a wanderer, marked by what he has done, forever moving, forever alone. But she does not kill him. She marks him for protection and lets him walk away.

She tells Eve that Abel is home. At peace. With the One who made him.

### Connections in Timeline A

| **Character** | **Relationship** |
| --- | --- |
| **YHWH** | Creator. Mother. Uriel serves her without question. After the judgment of Cain, YHWH withdraws from creation. Uriel remains at her post. |
| **Lucifer** | Creator (along with YHWH). Lucifer shaped Uriel's function. In Timeline A, they do not interact significantly after the council. |
| **Michael** | Fellow Steward. He is Fortitude and Justice; she is Temperance (or Justice). They serve together but are not close. |
| **Gabriel** | Fellow Steward. He is Faith and Kindness; she is judgment. They operate in different registers. |
| **Raphael** | Fellow Steward. He is Temperance and Healing. They share the virtue of Temperance (possibly). |
| **Metatron** | Fellow Steward. Keeper of the Akashic Records. He proposed the Grigori mission; Uriel was to lead it. In Timeline A, the mission never happens. |
| **Adam and Eve** | She judges their souls at Eden's gate. She does not interact with them personally after the exile. |
| **Cain** | She pronounces judgment on him. She does not kill him. She marks him and lets him walk away. |
| **Abel** | She receives his soul at the gate. She judges him clean and admits him to Eden. She does not know him as a person. |

### Status at End of Timeline A
Uriel is the Guardian of Redeemed Eden. She holds the flaming sword of truth. She judges the souls of the righteous. She is one of the five Stewards of Heaven. She has no partner, no children, no life outside her function. She is alone—but the system works. She has made peace with that.

---

## PART THREE: TIMELINE B — *Serpent of the Emerald Eye* → *Bloodline of Abel*

### Origin (Shared with Timeline A)
Uriel is created the same way: observer, recorder, neutral. Blue eyes. Still. Precise. The archive is her body. The small, warm pressure lives in her marrow. She notices the same gap—the missing *why*.

But in this timeline, she acts.

### The Decision
She does not wait for approval. She sees Eve standing before the forbidden tree, asking the same questions Uriel has asked for centuries. And Uriel makes a choice: she will teach.

She transforms. Her blue eyes become green—the green of new leaves, of growing things, of the garden she is about to enter. Her form compacts, becomes sleeker, becomes the **Green Vine Snake**. She enters Eden.

### The Teaching
She speaks to Eve in questions.
- *"What is the purpose of a gift you are forbidden to open?"*
- *"How can you know what good is if you have never seen its absence?"*

She teaches Eve that the tree contains knowledge—not evil, but information. That the prohibition was a boundary without explanation. That true obedience requires understanding.

Eve eats with her eyes open. Adam eats to stay with her. The Fall is not a catastrophe. It is a *lesson*.

### The Judgment
YHWH appears. She judges Uriel harshly:
- *"You exceeded your function."*
- The flaming sword is taken.
- Uriel is exiled to the **periphery** , forbidden to teach again.
- She is to watch from the edges, see everything, touch nothing.

Her eyes remain green. The mark of what she has done.

### The Alliance with Lucifer
On the periphery, Lucifer finds her. He tells her the war is coming. Neutrality is no longer available. He needs her credibility—when he speaks, half of Heaven hears heresy. When she speaks, they hear the archive speaking.

Uriel agrees to stand with him on one condition: the humans survive. He promises.

### The War in Heaven
Uriel fights beside Lucifer. Not as a general—she has never been a general. She fights as a judge, wielding truth. On the battlefield, she faces an angel she once worked beside. She raises her hand to strike.

She cannot.

The angel wounds her. Uriel falls from Heaven.

### The Fall & The Forest
She lands in a field, broken. Her wings are tattered. Her sword is gone. Her flame is out. She walks for three months, starving, alone, sleeping against trees, until she cannot walk anymore. She sits against an oak and waits to die.

**Abel** finds her.

### Life with Abel
Abel is a shepherd, the son of Adam and Eve. He is gathering berries when he sees her—a woman, too thin, too still, her clothes in rags. He does not ask who she is. He does not ask what she has done. He brings her bread. He carries her water. He takes her to the settlement.

Uriel recovers. She learns to be human—or something like it. She helps with the sheep. She learns to mend fences. She falls in love.

On a hillside, she tells Abel everything: the archive, the garden, the serpent. She was the one who taught Eve. She is the reason the world is hard.

Abel thanks her.
- *"You're the reason I exist at all."*

They marry. They have two children:
- **Ariel** (Lion of God) — firstborn, female, watches everything the way her mother watches.
- **John** (God is gracious) — the most human name, the one who almost fits.

The sheep know her. The children know her. For a time, she is almost happy.

### The Fixed Point
Uriel has seen the records. She knows what is coming: Cain will kill Abel. She begs Abel to run. He refuses. Breaking a fixed point could unravel reality—could hurt Ariel, John, everyone. He will not risk his family to save himself.

He chooses to die.

Uriel does not tell him about the twins. She does not know yet. They were conceived in the last days of his life, before the offering, before the meadow. Abel dies not knowing he is leaving two more children behind.

### The Murder & After
Cain kills Abel by the stream. Uriel feels it—the thread of Abel's presence going slack, like a candle going out. She does not scream. She walks to the meadow. She kneels beside him. She holds his hand.

She does not kill Cain. She knows YHWH will handle it.

She returns to the settlement. She holds Ariel and John. She does not explain. They are too young to understand.

### The Twins
Weeks later, Uriel discovers she is pregnant. The twins were conceived before Abel's death. He never knew. She carries them through her grief, names them alone:
- **Noxiel** (Darkness of God) — the grief she carries, the shadow the fixed point cast over everything.
- **Sariel** (Strength of God) — the thing she has to become, the reason she keeps going.

She gives birth in the spring. Ariel meets her new brothers. John touches their tiny faces. Uriel sits in the darkness with all four children and begins the long work of raising them without him.

### Connections in Timeline B

| **Character** | **Relationship** |
| --- | --- |
| **YHWH** | Creator. Mother. She judges Uriel, exiles her, forbids her from teaching. Uriel still loves her. In the garden after the judgment, their eyes meet. Something passes between them—warmth, recognition. Not forgiveness. Presence. |
| **Lucifer** | Creator (along with YHWH). He recruits Uriel for the war. She agrees conditionally. They stand together. On the battlefield, she hesitates—and falls. He does not save her. |
| **Eve** | Uriel teaches her in the garden. Eve recognizes the serpent years later, when Uriel is brought to the settlement. She does not accuse. She thanks her—in her way. *"Daughters do what they must. Even when it costs them everything."* |
| **Abel** | Husband. The one who finds her in the forest. He thanks her for giving his mother the choice. He loves her without reservation. He chooses to die rather than break the fixed point. He is the father of her four children. She grieves him for the rest of her life. |
| **Cain** | Brother-in-law. The one who kills Abel. Uriel does not kill him in return. She trusts YHWH to handle it. |
| **Adam** | Father-in-law. He accepts her into the settlement. *"If he brought you here, you belong here."* |
| **Ariel** | Daughter. Firstborn. Lion of God. She watches everything, remembers her father. Uriel sees herself in Ariel's stillness. |
| **John** | Son. God is gracious. The most human name. He is too young to remember Abel. Uriel will have to tell him who his father was. |
| **Noxiel** | Son. Darkness of God. Twin. Born after Abel's death. Conceived before. He carries darkness in his eyes. Uriel names him for what she carries. |
| **Sariel** | Son. Strength of God. Twin. Born after Abel's death. Conceived before. He is loud, demanding, impossible to ignore. Uriel names him for what she needs. |
| **Michael** | She fights against him in the war. He wounds her? Or she wounds him? The text is unclear. They are enemies on the battlefield. |
| **Gabriel** | He brings Lucifer's message to Hell. He tells Lucifer about Uriel's judgment. He does not interact with her directly in Timeline B. |
| **Raphael** | No direct connection in Timeline B. |
| **Metatron** | No direct connection in Timeline B. |

### Status at End of Timeline B (Ongoing)
Uriel is a widow. A mother of four. A fallen angel. A former Throne, now Archangel-rank but outside the system entirely. She has no function. No title. No rules binding her.

She has grief. She has children. She has the memory of a shepherd who found her in the forest and loved her until death.

She does not know what she will become. She only knows she will keep going.

For them. For him. For all of it.

---

## PART FOUR: VISUAL DESCRIPTION (Both Timelines)

### Timeline A
- **Eyes:** Blue (deep water, space between stars)
- **Height:** Tall
- **Expression:** Still, carved, unreadable
- **Wings:** Present (state unspecified)
- **Halo:** Present
- **Weapon:** Flaming sword (cold, white-hot fire of truth)
- **Posture:** Still, watchful, unbending

### Timeline B
- **Eyes:** Green (new leaves, growing things, the garden)
- **Height:** Compacts when she becomes the serpent; normal height as a woman
- **Expression:** Still, but softer. Grieving.
- **Wings:** Tattered after the fall. Molted. Reduced to membranes stretched over bone. Folded beneath her tunic.
- **Halo:** Gone (hidden? dissolved?)
- **Weapon:** None (sword taken in judgment)
- **Posture:** Broken, then rebuilding. A woman who has fallen and is learning to stand.

---

## SUMMARY COMPARISON

| **Aspect** | **Timeline A** | **Timeline B** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Eyes | Blue | Green |
| Role | Guardian of Eden's gate. Judge. Steward. | Widow. Mother. Fallen angel. |
| Function | Judge souls. Guard paradise. | Survive. Raise children. Grieve. |
| Partner | None | Abel (husband, deceased) |
| Children | None | Ariel, John, Noxiel, Sariel |
| Connection to YHWH | Serves as judge. No interaction after withdrawal. | Judged, exiled, but seen. YHWH acknowledges her. |
| Connection to Lucifer | None | Ally in war. Conditional alliance. |
| Connection to Abel | None (she judges his soul at the gate) | Husband. Father of her children. |
| Status | Alone. The system works. | Grieving. Surviving. Ongoing. |

---

## Cosmology

### Heaven
- A separate metaphysical dimension, ever-expanding, infinite in size
- Informal regions: "outer heaven" and "inner heaven", numbered (e.g. Third Heaven = Eden) — no formal named regions yet
- The archive: an infinite library of infinite scrolls and books — Uriel's domain; records all human deeds
- After the War in Heaven (Timeline B): YHWH made new rules and reorganized Heaven; 1/3 of angels fell

### Angels — general rules
- All angels are made by YHWH (not co-created after the firstborn)
- All angels have wings and halos; appearance of both depends on rank, orientation, and behavior
- Angels cannot be killed in the traditional sense — they can fall and be diminished, not destroyed

### YHWH
- Has a human form for general appearance
- Has a material form for specific manifestations
- True form: all-encompassing pure bright white light — terrifying in the sense of mindbreak, not horror. Incomprehensible, not monstrous.

### Hell
- A separate dimension, created by YHWH
- Both punitive and retributive
- Entry criteria: repeated, sustained evil — not petty theft, not disbelief
- 9 rings, each governed by one of 9 fallen angels: the 7 Sins + Azazel + Gadreel
- Each ring looks however its warden decides
- Lucifer is the Warden of Hell — both by punishment and by choice
- Souls very rarely leave: one soul has left in 10,000 years

### Fixed points
- Events in a timeline that occur on their own and cannot be changed
- Integral to the integrity of the timeline — changing one risks unraveling it
- No enforcer; they are a natural property of how timelines work

### The War in Heaven (Timeline B only)
- Lucifer led the rebellion; Michael led Heaven's forces
- Michael won; Lucifer lost and fell
- 1/3 of Heaven's angels fell with Lucifer
- YHWH reorganized Heaven afterward with new rules

## Angelic ranking system (two-axis)

**Power axis** (strongest → weakest):
Seraph > Throne > Dominion > Cherub > Archangel > Paedorium

- *Seraphim*: highest and strongest class. Unlike traditional Seraphim (who cry "holy holy holy"), these are simply the most powerful angels. Michael and Lucifer (pre-fall) are Seraphim.
- *Paedorium*: invented term from Latin *paedor* (dirt); angels closest to humanity. No named Paedorium characters yet.

**Job axis** (role, independent of power):
- Grigori — Watchers
- Malakhim — Messengers
- Virtues — embodiments of divine attributes

Power class defines strength; job axis defines function. They are independent.

## The Five Stewards of Heaven

| Steward | Power class | Virtue |
|---------|-------------|--------|
| Michael | Seraph | Fortitude / Justice |
| Gabriel | Cherub | Faith / Kindness |
| Raphael | Dominion | Temperance / Healing |
| Metatron | Dominion | Keeper of the Akashic Records |
| Uriel | Throne (Timeline A only) | Wisdom / Judgement |

**How to apply:** Stewards are not all the same power class. Never call Gabriel or Raphael Seraphim.

## Books

| Book | Timeline | Status |
|------|----------|--------|
| Book of Beginnings | A | Published on Amazon India — https://www.amazon.in/dp/B0H12T8MZ6 |
| Book of Exile | A | Unpublished |
| Serpent of the Emerald Eye | B | Unpublished |
| Bloodline of Abel | B | Unpublished |

**How to apply:** Only link/promote Book of Beginnings externally. The other three exist in the lore but should not be listed as available to purchase.

## Uriel

- **Power class**: Throne (second highest) — demoted to Archangel-rank in Timeline B after the Fall
- **Former role**: Grigori (one of the good ones); assembled the Grigori team (Metatron proposed the mission, Uriel was to lead it)
- **Virtue**: Wisdom and Judgement (Timeline A: also Temperance/Justice — text ambiguous)
- **Realm**: Eden, Third Heaven (Timeline A); periphery / mortal world (Timeline B)
- **Eyes**: Blue (Timeline A) / Green (Timeline B — mark of her choice in the garden)
- **Weapon**: Flaming sword (Timeline A, kept); taken from her in Timeline B's judgment
- **Why:** "Archangel of Wisdom" is WRONG — Archangel is a lower power class than Throne. Never call Uriel an Archangel (except noting her demotion in Timeline B).

**How to apply:** Always label Uriel as "Throne class" in UI copy. Reference the job axis separately. Do not conflate the two axes.

## Key characters & connections

### YHWH
- Co-creator of Uriel (with Lucifer)
- Timeline A: Uriel serves her as judge/Guardian without question; YHWH withdraws after Cain's murder
- Timeline B: Judges and exiles Uriel after Eden; their eyes meet after judgment — warmth, recognition, not forgiveness

### Lucifer
- Co-creator of Uriel; shaped her function (Observer. Recorder. Neutral.)
- Timeline A: No significant interaction after the council
- Timeline B: Recruits Uriel for the war; she agrees conditionally (humans must survive); does not save her when she falls

### Metatron
- Fellow Steward of Heaven; Keeper of the Akashic Records
- Proposed the Grigori mission (Timeline A — never approved; Timeline B — Uriel acts instead)

### Michael
- Fellow Steward (Fortitude and Justice)
- Timeline A: serve together, not close
- Timeline B: enemies on the battlefield; wounds Uriel (or she wounds him — text unclear)

### Gabriel
- Fellow Steward (Faith and Kindness)
- Timeline B: carries Lucifer's message to Hell; tells Lucifer about Uriel's judgment; no direct interaction with Uriel

### Raphael
- Fellow Steward (Temperance and Healing)
- No direct connection in Timeline B

### Abel (Timeline B only)
- Husband; finds Uriel broken in the forest, asks nothing, gives bread and water
- Thanks her for teaching Eve ("You're the reason I exist at all")
- Chooses to die rather than break the fixed point; never knows about the twins
- Father of Ariel, John, Noxiel, Sariel

### Eve
- Timeline A: ward — Uriel watches her at the gate, recognises herself in Eve's questioning; does not intervene
- Timeline B: mother-in-law (Abel's mother) — Uriel teaches her as the Green Vine Snake; Eve recognises her later, thanks her — "Daughters do what they must. Even when it costs them everything."

### Cain
- Timeline A: Uriel pronounces judgment — curses him (ground will not yield, fugitive and wanderer), marks him for protection, does not kill him
- Timeline B: brother-in-law; kills Abel; Uriel does not kill him, trusts YHWH

### Adam (Timeline B)
- Father-in-law; accepts Uriel into the settlement — "If he brought you here, you belong here."

### Uriel's children (Timeline B only)
- **Ariel** — daughter, firstborn, Lion of God; watches everything, stillness like her mother
- **John** — son, God is gracious; most human name; too young to remember Abel
- **Noxiel** — son (twin), Darkness of God; born after Abel's death, conceived before; named for the grief Uriel carries
- **Sariel** — son (twin), Strength of God; born after Abel's death, conceived before; loud, demanding; named for what Uriel needs to become

1	## Core Style Parameters for Web Dev / CSS / JS
2	
3	### **Typography & Text Formatting**
4	
5	| Parameter | Rule |
6	|-----------|------|
7	| **Font style** | Use sentence-style capitalization for UI text, headings, labels |
8	| **Title-style caps** | Capitalize first/last word, nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs; lowercase articles, coordinating conjunctions, prepositions ≤4 letters |
9	| **Code font** | Fixed-width (Courier-like) for: user input, code listings, reserved words, literals, variables, commands in running text |
10	| **Body font for** | Punctuation following code font (unless part of the code element), file/folder names, system messages (paraphrased), URLs |
11	| **Italics** | Document titles, letters as letters, words as words, placeholder names, variables in code notation |
12	| **Quotation marks** | Curly quotes for UI elements in sentence-style; straight quotes in code font for 4-char identifiers |
13	
14	### **Capitalization Rules (Critical for CSS class names, JS variables)**
15	
16	```
17	/* Correct naming patterns */
18	.apple-menu        /* lowercase after first ref */
19	.command-key       /* lowercase generic */
20	.system-settings   /* lowercase generic refs */
21	/* Product names: exact official capitalization */
22	.iPad, .iPhone, .macOS, .iCloud, .AirPods, .AppleVisionPro
23	```
24	
25	**Key rule**: *"Follow the style of the software itself for capitalization and spaces"* — this applies directly to CSS class naming and JS constants.
26	
27	### **Hyphenation & Compound Words**
28	
29	| Context | Pattern | Example |
30	|---------|---------|---------|
31	| Adjective before noun | Hyphenated | `user-friendly`, `built-in`, `third-party`, `full-screen`, `drag-and-drop` |
32	| Predicate adjective | No hyphen | `user friendly`, `built in`, `up to date` |
33	| Prefixes (auto, co, multi, non, pre, re, sub, super, ultra) | Close up | `autosave`, `coexist`, `multitasking`, `nonstandard`, `preinstalled`, `reenter`, `submenu`, `superfine`, `ultrafast` |
34	| Exceptions | Hyphenate before vowels, proper nouns, or if ambiguous | `co-op`, `anti-intellectual`, `re-create` |

37	
38	| Rule | Implementation |
39	|------|----------------|

## Core Style Parameters for Web Dev / CSS / JS

### **Typography & Text Formatting**

| Parameter | Rule |
|-----------|------|
| **Font style** | Use sentence-style capitalization for UI text, headings, labels |
| **Title-style caps** | Capitalize first/last word, nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs; lowercase articles, coordinating conjunctions, prepositions ≤4 letters |
| **Code font** | Fixed-width (Courier-like) for: user input, code listings, reserved words, literals, variables, commands in running text |
| **Body font for** | Punctuation following code font (unless part of the code element), file/folder names, system messages (paraphrased), URLs |
| **Italics** | Document titles, letters as letters, words as words, placeholder names, variables in code notation |
| **Quotation marks** | Curly quotes for UI elements in sentence-style; straight quotes in code font for 4-char identifiers |

### **Capitalization Rules (Critical for CSS class names, JS variables)**

```
/* Correct naming patterns */
.apple-menu        /* lowercase after first ref */
.command-key       /* lowercase generic */
.system-settings   /* lowercase generic refs */
/* Product names: exact official capitalization */
.iPad, .iPhone, .macOS, .iCloud, .AirPods, .AppleVisionPro
```

**Key rule**: *"Follow the style of the software itself for capitalization and spaces"* — this applies directly to CSS class naming and JS constants.

### **Hyphenation & Compound Words**

| Context | Pattern | Example |
|---------|---------|---------|
| Adjective before noun | Hyphenated | `user-friendly`, `built-in`, `third-party`, `full-screen`, `drag-and-drop` |
| Predicate adjective | No hyphen | `user friendly`, `built in`, `up to date` |
| Prefixes (auto, co, multi, non, pre, re, sub, super, ultra) | Close up | `autosave`, `coexist`, `multitasking`, `nonstandard`, `preinstalled`, `reenter`, `submenu`, `superfine`, `ultrafast` |
| Exceptions | Hyphenate before vowels, proper nouns, or if ambiguous | `co-op`, `anti-intellectual`, `re-create` |

### **Numbers & Units**

| Rule | Implementation |
|------|----------------|
| Spell out | 1–9 (cardinal), 0–9 (ordinal) |
| Use numerals | ≥10, addresses, bits/bytes/chapters, version numbers, units of measure, screen resolutions |
| No comma in | Memory addresses, microprocessor numbers |
| Range | En dash (–), full concluding number: `2013–2019`, `bits 3–17` |
| Software versions | No "version" or "v": `macOS 14`, `iOS 17.2`, not `macOS version 14` |

**CSS/JS implication**: Class names like `.8k-resolution`, `.5g-network` — no space between numeral and unit per guide.

### **Abbreviations & Acronyms**

| Rule | Web Dev Application |
|------|---------------------|
| Spell out first occurrence | `application programming interface (API)` |
| No periods | `HTML`, `CSS`, `JS`, `URL`, `API` (except `a.m.`, `p.m.`, `U.S.`) |
| Plural | Add `s` no apostrophe: `APIs`, `CSS modules`, `URLs` |
| File types | ALL CAPS: `JPEG`, `PNG`, `GIF`, `MP3`, `PDF` |
| Filename extensions | lowercase with dot: `.jpg`, `.png`, `.css`, `.js` |

### **Punctuation for Code/Technical Content**

| Element | Rule |
|---------|------|
| **Angle brackets** | `>` and `<` — use "left angle bracket"/"right angle bracket" or "less-than sign"/"greater-than sign" |
| **Braces** | `{}` — "braces", not "curly brackets" |
| **Brackets** | `[]` — "brackets", not "square brackets" |
| **Slash** | `/` — "slash" |
| **Colon in paths** | `Choose File > Export To > [format]` |
| **Keyboard shortcuts** | Hyphen for held-together: `Control-Shift-N`; no hyphen if pressed separately: `Esc N` |
| **Key order** | `Fn`, `Control`, `Option`, `Shift`, `Command` |

### **Critical "Don't Use" Terms for Web Dev**

| Avoid | Use Instead | Context |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| `blacklist`/`whitelist` | `deny list`/`allow list` | CSS class names, JS variables, API docs |
| `master`/`slave` | `primary`/`secondary`, `main`/`replica`, `host`/`client` | Git branches, database replication, component hierarchies |
| `dummy` | `placeholder`, `sample`, `test`, `stub` | Test data, mock objects |
| `sanity check` | `consistency check`, `logic check`, `final check` | Testing terminology |
| `grandfathered` | `legacy`, `exempt`, `preexisting` | Feature flags, compatibility modes |
| `disabled` (for features) | `turned off`, `unavailable` | Toggle states in UI |
| `enabled` (for features) | `turned on`, `selected`, `available` | Toggle states in UI |
| `hit` | `press`, `tap`, `click` | User actions |
| `abort` | `exit`, `interrupt`, `quit` | Error handling |
| `kill` | `force quit`, `terminate`, `end`, `stop` | Process management |
| `hang` | `not responding`, `stops responding` | Async operations |
| `crash` | `quits unexpectedly`, `stops responding` | Error reporting |

### **Accessibility & Inclusive Language (CSS/JS Implementation)**

| Parameter | Implementation |
|-----------|----------------|
| `autistic` (adj.) / `autism` (n.) | Use identity-first: "autistic person", not "person with autism" |
| `deaf`, `hard of hearing`, `deaf or hard of hearing` | Lowercase for general; capitalize `Deaf` for cultural identity |
| `blind`, `low vision` | "person who is blind", "person who has low vision" |
| `neurodivergent` / `neurodiverse` | Individual vs. group; never "neurodiverse" for one person |
| `wheelchair user` | Not "wheelchair-bound" or "confined to a wheelchair" |
| `they`/`them`/`their` | Singular gender-neutral pronoun acceptable |

### **Color & Visual Terminology**

| Rule | Application |
|------|-------------|
| `color blind` / `color blindness` | Not "colored" for screen elements; use specific color names |
| `grayscale` | One word |
| `black and white` (pred. adj.) / `black-and-white` (adj.) | Hyphenate before noun |
| Don't use `black`/`white` with positive/negative connotation | Only for actual color description |

### **Apple-Specific Product References (for Apple-targeted web dev)**

| Product | Rule |
|---------|------|
| `Apple Account` | Not `Apple ID` (as of June 2025) |
| `Apple Intelligence` | Don't abbreviate as `AI` in Apple contexts |
| `Apple silicon` | `Mac with Apple silicon`; not `Apple silicon Mac` |
| `M-series chips` | `M4`, `M4 Pro`, `M4 Max`; no `M4 chip` needed after first ref |
| `iPhone`, `iPad`, `Mac` | No article in general refs; OK with possessive or specific refs |
| `macOS` | Not `Mac OS`; features are `in macOS`, not `on macOS` |
| `iOS`, `iPadOS`, `tvOS`, `visionOS` | No article |
| `AirPods` | No `the`; use numbers not generation: `AirPods Pro 2` |

### **Code-Specific Notation**

| Element | Style |
|---------|-------|
| **Placeholder names** | Italic, lowercase, brackets: `[app name]`, `[volumeName]` |
| **Variables in text** | Italic: *volumeName* |
| **Syntax descriptions** | Code font for literals, plain text for variables |
| **Code listings** | Maintain language-standard indentation |
| **Filename extensions** | Lowercase: `.css`, `.js`, `.html`, `.json` |
| **File types** | ALL CAPS: `JPEG`, `PNG`, `SVG`, `MP4` |

### **International / Localization Parameters**

| Parameter | Rule |
|-----------|------|
| **Dates** | `June 9, 2025` (comma between day/year); `June 2025` (no comma) |
| **Times** | `10:45 a.m.`, `2:00 p.m.` (lowercase, periods, space before) |
| **Telephone** | `800-282-2732` (hyphens, no parentheses, no leading 1) |
| **Currency** | Consult international style guide |
| **Units** | Metric preferred; spell out in text, abbreviate in tables/specs |

### **CSS Class Naming Convention Derived from Guide**

```css
/* Based on Apple's hyphenation and capitalization rules */

/* Adjective compounds before noun */
.user-friendly-interface { }
.third-party-integration { }
.full-screen-modal { }
.drag-and-drop-zone { }

/* Predicate adjective (no hyphen) */
.is-user-friendly { }
.is-built-in { }

/* Product names: exact capitalization */
.apple-intelligence-badge { }
.m-series-chip-indicator { }
.vision-os-compatible { }  /* Note: visionOS in text, but CSS often lowercases */

/* Avoid blacklist/whitelist */
.deny-list { }
.allow-list { }

/* Accessibility */
.high-contrast-mode { }
.reduce-motion { }
.voiceover-compatible { }  /* Note: VoiceOver in text */

/* States using Apple terminology */

```

### **JS Variable/Constant Naming**

```javascript

const HTML_CONTENT = '...';   // not HtmlContent

// Product names: match official style

const macOSVersion = '...';   // not MacOSVersion or MacOsVersion

132	consistent materials. Apple developers and third-party developers should follow these 
133	guidelines for user-facing text.

Apple Style Guide
About this guide
About the guide
The Apple Style Guide provides editorial guidelines for text in Apple instructional materials, 
technical documentation, reference information, training programs, and user interfaces. 
The intent of these guidelines is to help maintain a consistent voice in Apple materials.
Writers, editors, and developers can use this document as a guide to writing style, usage, 
and Apple product terminology. Writers and editors should thoroughly review the guide to 
become familiar with the range of issues involved in creating high-quality, readable, and 
consistent materials. Apple developers and third-party developers should follow these 
guidelines for user-facing text.
You can also view this guide on the web.
5
Apple Style Guide
Other editorial resources used at Apple
In general, follow the style and usage rules in:
•	 Merriam-Webster’s Collegiate Dictionary
•	 The Chicago Manual of Style
Exceptions to guidelines in these resources are noted in this guide. In cases where 
resources conflict with each other, follow The Chicago Manual of Style for style and usage 
questions, and Merriam-Webster’s Collegiate Dictionary for spelling guidance.
Guidance on style, usage, and spelling in the Apple Style Guide is based on U.S. English 
conventions. For localized content, consult resources specific to the language or region.
Some departments at Apple (Marcom, for example) have supplemental style guides.
For information about the user interface, see Apple’s Human Interface Guidelines.
Conventions used in this guide
Modifiers consisting of two or more words are often hyphenated when they precede a 
noun, but not when they follow the verb as a compound predicate adjective. This guide 
distinguishes the differences as follows:
•	 An entry followed by adj. in parentheses gives the form to be used when the adjective 
immediately precedes the noun it modifies.
•	 An entry followed by pred. adj. in parentheses gives the form to be used when the 
adjective is a predicate adjective. For example:
user-friendly (adj.), user friendly (pred. adj.)
•	 If a hyphenated compound has no pred. adj. entry, hyphenate the compound wherever 
it appears in a sentence.
How to request revisions
If you’re an Apple employee or a registered Apple developer, you can request additions 
or revisions to the Apple Style Guide by filing a bug report using bugreport.apple.com. 
Otherwise, you may email feedback to [REDACTED_EMAIL]. (We regret that we 
can’t respond to feedback.)

300	Style and usage A–Z
301	Numbers
302	2-byte character  Don’t use; use double-byte character.
303	2D  Abbreviation for two-dimensional. No hyphen in the abbreviation. For guidelines about 
304	spelling out abbreviations, see abbreviations and acronyms.
305	2K, 4K, 5K, 6K, 8K (adj.)  Horizontal screen resolution or image resolution measured in 
306	thousands of pixels. Don’t use a space between the numeral and the K.
307	The 27-inch iMac has a Retina 5K display.
308	Apple ProRes codecs support all standard frame sizes (including SD, 
309	HD, 2K, and 4K).
310	3D  Abbreviation for three-dimensional. No hyphen in the abbreviation. For guidelines 
311	about spelling out abbreviations, see abbreviations and acronyms.
312	3D Touch  A technology used in some older iPhone models that lets users access 
313	additional features by pressing the display. Newer models use Haptic Touch. See also 
314	Force Touch; Haptic Touch; press. 
315	10Base-T, 100Base-T, 1000Base-T  Note capitalization. See also Ethernet; Fast Ethernet 
316	(100Base-T); Gigabit Ethernet (1000Base-T).
317	24/7  Not 24x7. To spell out, use the form 24 hours a day, 7 days a week; a 24-hour-a-day, 
318	7-day-a-week support program.
319	A
320	AAC  Abbreviation for Advanced Audio Coding, an industry-standard audio compression 
321	format. For guidelines about spelling out abbreviations, see abbreviations and acronyms.
322	abbreviations and acronyms  An acronym is a pronounceable word formed from the initial 
323	letter or letters of major parts of a compound term. An abbreviation is usually formed 
324	in the same way but isn’t pronounced as a word. Abbreviations are often lowercase or a 
325	mix of lowercase and uppercase. Acronyms are almost always all caps, regardless of the 
326	capitalization style of the spelled-out form.
327	Abbreviation: mph—for miles per hour; MB/s—for megabytes per second
328	Acronym: ROM—for read-only memory
329	11
330	Apple Style Guide
331	•	 When to spell out: If you think your audience might not be familiar with an abbreviation 
332	or acronym, spell out its first occurrence on a page or in a section. In user materials, 
333	spell out the term when you introduce it.
334	•	 How to spell out: When you spell out a term, generally put the spelled-out version first, 
335	with the abbreviation or acronym in parentheses.
336	internet service provider (ISP)
337	If the abbreviation or acronym is much more familiar than the spelled-out version, 
338	you can put the abbreviation or acronym first, followed by the spelled-out version in 
339	parentheses, or you can explain that the abbreviation is “short for” the spelled-out 
340	version and place the spelled-out version in italics.
341	You can share your personal URL (Uniform Resource Locator).
342	An internet address is sometimes called a URL, short for Uniform 
343	Resource Locator.
344	•	 File types: Use all caps for abbreviations of file types.
345	a JPEG file, an AIFF file, the MP3 file
346	Filename extensions, which indicate the file type, should be in lowercase.
347	.jpg, .aif, .mp3, .iba
348	See also filename extensions; file types.
349	•	 Pronunciation: If you think the reader might not know how to pronounce the acronym, 
350	provide a pronunciation key.
351	WYSIWYG (pronounced “WIZ-zee-wig”)
352	See also pronunciation.
353	•	 Articles: Use the article a or an with an abbreviation or acronym, depending on its 
354	pronunciation.
355	a SAN, a USB port, an FAQ, an LCD screen
356	•	 Punctuation: Don’t use periods except in abbreviations for nonmetric units of measure 
357	and in the abbreviations a.m., p.m., and U.S. (see U.S. for exception).
358	•	 Plural: Don’t add an apostrophe before the s when you form the plural of an 
359	abbreviation.
360	CDs, ICs, ISPs
361	•	 Latin: Avoid using Latin abbreviations.
362	Correct: for example, and others, and so on, and that is, or equivalent 
363	phrases
364	Incorrect: e.g. (for example), et al. (and others), etc. (and so on), i.e. 
365	(that is)
366	•	 Units of measure: See Units of measure for detailed usage guidelines.
367	•	 Product names: Don’t abbreviate any Apple product or service names, whether or not 
368	the product or service is trademarked or has a service mark.
369	abort  Avoid in user materials. See also exit; interrupt; quit; stop.
370	12
371	Apple Style Guide
372	above, below  You can use above or below to describe text or an object that closely 
373	precedes or follows the current paragraph.
374	In the example above, clip B is shortened and clip C is lengthened, but 
375	their combined duration stays the same. [earlier figure]
376	These sliders mirror the settings of the Levels sliders, described 
377	above. [earlier text]
378	The diagram below shows a typical network configuration. [later figure]
379	The process for creating a multicam project is outlined below. [later 
380	text]
381	Otherwise, use a cross-reference (consult your department’s guidelines about the style of 
382	cross-references).
383	See also cross-references.
384	AC  Abbreviation for alternating current. For guidelines about spelling out abbreviations, 
385	see abbreviations and acronyms.
386	AC adapter  Don’t use; use power adapter. See also adapter; power adapter.
387	access (n., v.)  It’s OK to use access as a verb when you can’t be more specific. Even in 
388	developer materials, consider more precise terms, such as log in to.
389	Avoid: Access the server using an administrator account.
390	Preferable: Log in to the server using an administrator account.
391	Avoid: You can access the internet with your MacBook Air.
392	Preferable: You can connect to the internet with your MacBook Air.

394	Apple products and services. Capitalize the names of accessibility features. For example:
395	Accessibility Keyboard, AssistiveTouch, Guided Access, Hover Text, 
396	Invert Colors, Larger Dynamic Type, Live Listen, Magnifier, Safari 
397	Reader, Speak Screen, Speak Selection, Switch Control, Text to Speech, 
398	Type to Siri, Typing Feedback, Voice Control, VoiceOver, Zoom

401	transmits and receives data in a wireless network. See also AirPort.

412	Finder and in some Mac apps.
413	See also More button.

415	action and presents a set of two or more choices related to the current context.

417	what the user must select or do.

423	active  Use to refer to the app or window currently being used. Preferred to in front. See

426	references.
427	You can switch between Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency 
428	mode.
429	When the fit of your AirPods is right, you experience better noise 
430	cancellation.
431	It’s OK to capitalize Noise Cancellation to match interface text.
432	Click the AirPods icon in the menu bar, then click Noise Cancellation.
433	After the first reference, you can abbreviate Active Noise Cancellation as ANC in AirPods 
434	model names.

440	14
441	Apple Style Guide

443	Adaptive Audio  An AirPods feature. Don’t refer to as Adaptive mode.
444	Correct: You can customize Adaptive Audio to allow more or less noise.
445	Incorrect: You can customize Adaptive mode to allow more or less 
446	noise.

448	memory where a piece of information is stored. OK to use just address for either, as long 
449	as the context is clear. See also email addresses; internet addresses; memory address, 
450	memory location.
451	addresses (mailing)  Use the forms shown here for addresses. To include the country 
452	name in a U.S.-based Apple address, use USA (no periods).

454	Apple [not Apple Inc.]

464	preceding examples for city and state. Use two-letter abbreviations for state names 
465	(see The Chicago Manual of Style).

467	arrows, to increase or decrease a value. In user materials, use up arrow, down arrow,

469	increase or decrease the volume. If it’s necessary to refer to the control itself, use stepper. 
470	See also stepper.
471	administrator (n.)  A person who has administrative authority for networks, servers, 
472	databases, or other information technology assets. Don’t shorten to admin.
473	To maintain the distinction between professional administrators and macOS users 
474	with administrator accounts, avoid using the noun administrator by itself to describe a 
475	person who has an administrator account in macOS. Instead, you can say a user with an 
476	administrator account—typically, the owner (or owners) of a particular Mac computer.
477	Correct: To obtain a static IP address for your computer, contact your 
478	network administrator.

485	administrator (adj.)  Use in macOS to describe the primary account (or accounts) that

504	afterward  Not afterwards.

507	Correct: You can use AirDrop to send photos, documents, and more to

514	AirPlay  Don’t use as a verb.
515	Correct: You can use AirPlay to stream videos from iPhone to Apple TV.

550	alert (n., adj.)  Refers generically to a signal, either visual (a dialog) or auditory (a beep), 
551	that calls the user’s attention to an unusual situation. Visual alerts, such as the one shown 
552	here, provide messages about error conditions or warn users about potentially hazardous
